Senses.Note: The one-mark complete command is described as not dwelling in marks and not producing grasping or aversion within them. Later speakers raise the inherited name and demand its present expression.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The one-mark complete command is described as not dwelling in marks and not producing grasping or aversion within them. Later speakers raise the inherited name and demand its present expression.
EvidenceBody: A technical compound is made observable through conduct amid marks and through public questions asking what the one mark is here.
Three witnesses transmit Huineng’s same definition in different works; the fourth is a later independent deployment, so repetition is not mistaken for four definitions.
